pages.text: The Sample Collector is the $(reset)starting point$(reset) of the whole line: hold it and right-click a creature to draw a Life Sample.$(br2)$(bold)How to use:$(reset)$(li)Right-click a life-energy block/pipe to charge: it stores 100,000 and each draw costs 5,000 — 20 draws per full charge$(li)Success = the creature group's base rate + a wounded bonus: +10 below 50% HP, another +10 below 25%, capped at 95%$(li)On failure you keep half the energy, but the sample is lost$(li)Each creature yields at most 3 successful samples$(br2)$(bold)Purity:$(reset) draws are random — about 60% land in the 0-49 bracket, which the Cultivator can $(reset)refine$(reset) later.$(br2)Sampling tip: reduce the target to low health before drawing.

pages.title: Creature Groups
pages.text: $(bold)Your group decides a sample's potential:$(reset)$(br2)$(li)$(reset)Warm-blooded$(reset) (farm animals, fish...): base purity 45, collect rate 85%$(li)$(reset)Undead$(reset) (zombies, skeletons...): 55 / 70%$(li)$(reset)Explosive$(reset) (creeper): 60 / 55%$(li)$(reset)Aberrant$(reset) (spiders, slimes, blazes...): 65 / 45%$(li)$(reset)Ender$(reset) (endermen, shulkers...): 70 / 40%$(li)$(reset)Boss$(reset) (wither, warden): 85 / 20%$(li)$(reset)Dragon$(reset) (ender dragon): 90 / 25%$(br2)Matching order: Dragon ＞ Boss ＞ Explosive ＞ Aberrant ＞ Ender ＞ Undead ＞ Warm-blooded.$(br2)Low purity yields only low-grade organs; raise purity by sampling stronger creatures or refining in the Cultivator.

The Gene Analyzer $(reset)deconstructs$(reset) a sample of purity 25+ into a Gene Sequence Fragment.$(br2)$(bold)Costs:$(reset)$(li)100 ticks (5 seconds) and 5,000 life energy$(li)Success scales linearly with purity: roughly 70% at purity 25, up to about 95% at purity 100$(li)Win or lose, the sample is always consumed$(br2)Samples below purity 25 cannot be processed; refine them at the Cultivator first.$(br2)This machine is the line's bottleneck: without sequences the later stages stop.

A Gene Sequence Fragment is the feedstock of the Structuring Table, and it $(reset)keeps the creature source and purity$(reset).$(br2)Hand it to the "$(l:akaishi:life_struct)Life Structuring Table$(/l)" to forge an organ.$(br2)$(bold)Purity determines value:$(reset) higher purity means higher organ integrity, while samples and sequences below 25 are barely worth keeping.$(br2)Store extra stock in the "Sample Vault" described under "$(l:akaishi:life_vaults)Vaults$(/l)"; purity also unlocks trait tiers — see "$(l:akaishi:trait_safe)Safe Mutations$(/l)".

Suggested order: read "$(l:akaishi:life_struct)Life Structuring Table$(/l)" to forge sequences into organs; vault your spare samples and sequences; trait mechanics are covered in the Mutations chapter.
